newsitem.title: USA: U.S. firefighters battle blaze that razed 34 homes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firefighters battle blaze that razed 34 homes.

text.p: Hundreds of firefighters battled on Saturday to hold back a fierce Montana forest fire that has destroyed 34 homes and threatened a dozen more, officials said.

The Shepard Mountain fire, burning in rugged terrain in the Custer National Forest of southern Montana, suddenly flared up earlier this week from a small fire to an inferno that raced through the dry forest.

The lightning-caused fire, burning about 20 miles (30 km) west of the town of Red Lodge, had reached 12,800 acres (5,200 hectares) by Saturday, leaving a trail of destroyed summer homes in its wake. Thirty-four homes and three outbuildings were confirmed lost, fire information officer Dixie Dies said.
The destroyed homes were not simple wooden cabins, she said. "We're talking some pretty nice places. It's a home I'd live in in a heartbeat," she said.

The fire still threatened about a dozen other homes at the bottom of a steep canyon, Dies said. Some 500 firefighters were battling the blaze, backed up by an air tanker and seven helicopters dropping water and fire retardant, she said.

About 50 evacuated residents of the small communities of Roscoe and Luther were being allowed to go back on Saturday because their homes were no longer in danger, Dies said. About 60 residents of another subdivision remained evacuated.
Firefighters did not have fire lines around any of the fire and had no estimate of when it would be fully contained.
There were fears that winds would pick up on Saturday afternoon, fanning the flames.
Two firefighters were injured, one suffering second-degree burns, when the fire flared up earlier this week.

Elsewhere, firefighters made steady progress against fires burning in four western states. The National Interagency Fire Centre, based in Boise, Idaho, said 8,500 firefighters were battling eight major fires burning on 185,000 acres (75,000 hectares) in Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Wyoming.

The troublesome Stockwell fire in Wyoming's Big Horn National Forest swelled to 2,840 acres (1,150 hectares) and was only 10 percent contained, fire officials said. But four big blazes in Oregon were nearing full containment.

The Western United States is having its worst fire season in 30 years, with fires spreading quickly in parched grass, brush and forest. More than 5.8 million acres (2.3 million hectares) have burned so far this year, compared with a five-year average of 2.1 million acres (850,000 hectares).
